name: Code2Database
description: Scan C/C++/Go/Python/Java/Rust/ASM codebases and generate a persistent directed code graph with invocation ordering, conditions, conditional compilation paths (#ifdef), concurrency analysis, data race detection, field-level access tracking, confidence classification, and evidence traces. Query with one tool call instead of grep/glob/Read. Capabilities: commit-based provenance with git hash verification (engineers verify with `git show <hash>`, not timestamps), Cypher-subset query language (MATCH/WHERE/RETURN), value flow with DATA_FLOW edges, lock-held region analysis with event-stream char positions, Z3 SMT path feasibility checking, cross-function data dependency (DATA_DEP) edges, invariant extraction (preconditions/postconditions/loop_invariants/state_machine), LLM auto-semantic enhancement with confidence-threshold auto-write and batch-confirm/rollback, transactional updates with WAL and snapshots via fcntl file locks, cross-language FFI tracing (Python ctypes/Go cgo/Rust extern C), interactive Web UI with single-file HTML/SVG/JS, BUG benchmark (GraphInvestigator vs GrepInvestigator recall/precision/tool-calls/tokens/time), profile health scoring (0-100 across 7 categories) with auto-evolution and git/svn HEAD binding, doc-code dual-source truth alignment (detect return value / param / signature / stale-doc mismatches; describe-node surfaces doc_code_mismatches; knowledge-validate includes doc-code alignment), a background daemon with inotify + polling fallback, Unix socket API (/tmp/code2database-daemon-<project>.sock), circuit breaker, transactional sync, and auto output file rebuild, plus a cgdb (code graph database) layer with dual clang+tree-sitter backend (typed vtable dispatch, CFG, data flow, alias analysis, sync primitives, config predicates, ops bindings, time-travel version queries). Use when user asks about code invocation relationships, function invocation chains, invocation ordering, conditional invoke paths, conditional compilation effects, architecture domain structure, API entry points, external endpoint classification, concurrency risks, data races, invariants, FFI boundaries, doc-code consistency, or wants to generate/visualize a code graph — especially when code2db-out/ exists. Not for: writing unit tests, simple single-file lookups, or general questions unrelated to invocation relationships.
